stories.headline: Apple Holds Exploratory Talks With Intel and Samsung to Build Device Chips in the US

key_facts.fact: Apple has held early-stage talks with Intel about enlisting its chipmaking services, and Apple executives have visited a Samsung plant under development in Texas for advanced chip production.
The move would offer a secondary option beyond longtime partner TSMC, which has been Apple's sole fabrication partner for over a decade using 3-nanometer process technology.
Recent chip shortages driven by AI data center build-out and higher-than-anticipated Mac demand have highlighted the need for supply diversification.
Intel and Samsung currently cannot reliably offer the type of production scale and consistency that TSMC provides to Apple.

stories.headline: Blackstone Files for $1.75B Data Center REIT IPO to Buy AI-Linked Properties

key_facts.fact: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust filed to raise $1.75 billion in an IPO, offering 87.5 million shares at $20 each on the NYSE under ticker BXDC.
The REIT will acquire newly constructed data centers valued between $250M and $1.5B that are leased to top investment-grade hyperscalers, targeting returns of 5.75% to 7% or higher.

Blackstone has executed $225B in data center transactions since 2018, including more than $150B in asset deals, and has flagged $25B in near-term acquisition targets across Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin.
A Blackstone affiliate plans to buy up to $200M of shares, and IPO investors will receive bonus shares equal to 1% of their purchase.
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan Chase, RBC Capital Markets, and Wells Fargo are managing the offering.

stories.headline: China Invokes Anti-Sanctions Law for First Time, Orders Companies to Defy US Blacklist on Oil Refiners

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce on May 2 ordered companies not to comply with US sanctions against five refiners, the first time Beijing has used its 2021 blocking rules
The five sanctioned refiners include Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian), Shandong Jincheng, Hebei Xinhai Chemical, Shandong Shengxing Chemical, and Shandong Shouguang Luqing
Under the law (revised April 2026), China can impose countermeasures on companies and individuals including trade, investment curbs and entry/exit restrictions
The move comes less than two weeks before Trump is due to visit Beijing on May 14-15 for a summit with Xi Jinping
A White House official warned: 'Any company considering skirting US sanctions should think twice'
Independent 'teapot' refiners in China are the main buyers of Iran's oil exports; Iran accounts for roughly 13% of China's oil imports and China for 90%+ of Iran's crude exports

stories.headline: Cisco Acquires Astrix Security for ~$400M to Secure AI Agents and Non-Human Identities

key_facts.fact: Cisco announced the acquisition of Israeli startup Astrix Security for approximately $400 million to bolster its AI agent security portfolio
Astrix specializes in securing non-human identities (NHIs) — API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens, and the credentials AI agents use to access systems at scale
According to Cisco's AI Readiness Index, only 24% of organizations can control AI agent actions with proper guardrails and live monitoring
Astrix was founded in 2021 by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour, veterans of Israel's Unit 8200, and raised $85 million in total prior to the deal
Cisco will integrate Astrix into Cisco Identity Intelligence, Secure Access, and Duo IAM, with data feeding into Splunk for unified agent activity monitoring

stories.headline: DeepInfra Raises $107M Series B Backed by Nvidia to Scale Open-Model Inference Cloud

key_facts.fact: DeepInfra raised $107 million in a Series B co-led by 500 Global and Georges Harik (one of Google's first cloud engineers), with participation from Nvidia, Samsung Next, and Supermicro
DeepInfra grew its token processing volume by 25x since its Series A, operating its own GPU infrastructure across eight US data centers
The platform currently supports 190+ open-weight models and uses Nvidia's Dynamo distributed-inference platform and Vera Rubin GPUs for 20x greater inference cost efficiency
DeepInfra argues inference, not training, is now the dominant AI workload constraint, with a single agentic task requiring 50 to 100+ model calls
The company was founded by the same team that built imo, a messaging app used by 200M+ people, bringing expertise in high-throughput distributed systems

stories.headline: FDA Approves Auvelity as First Non-Antipsychotic Treatment for Alzheimer's-Related Agitation

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Auvelity (dextromethorphan-bupropion) for treatment of agitation associated with Alzheimer's disease, making it the only FDA-approved non-antipsychotic for this indication
Auvelity works by modulating NMDA and sigma-1 receptors, a different mechanism from antipsychotic medications; it was already FDA-approved for major depressive disorder
Agitation affects roughly three-quarters of Alzheimer's patients and can include restless pacing to physically or verbally lashing out at others
Approval based on four Phase 3 studies (ACCORD, ACCORD-2, ADVANCE-1, ADVANCE-2) plus a long-term extension study; patients on placebo were more likely to relapse
Auvelity was the only FDA-approved product to show statistically significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms vs placebo in a long-term study

stories.headline: Global Chip Sales Hit $298.5B in Q1 2026, Up 25% QoQ, On Track for $1 Trillion Year

key_facts.fact: Global semiconductor sales were $298.5 billion in Q1 2026, up 25% from Q4 2025, with March sales of $99.5 billion up 79.2% year-over-year.
Asia Pacific/All Other led year-over-year growth at 108.5%, followed by the Americas at 83.1%, China at 74.8%, Europe at 46.5%, and Japan at 7.4%.
SIA president John Neuffer said global chip sales remain on track to reach $1 trillion in 2026.

Separately, SEMI reported global silicon wafer shipments rose 13.1% year-over-year in Q1 to 3,275 million square inches, driven by AI data center demand for advanced logic, memory, and power management devices.

Omdia projects global semiconductor market revenue will reach approximately $1.35 trillion this year, up 62.7% YoY, with a 32-point upward revision in just three months driven by memory chip price surges.

stories.headline: Intel Hires Qualcomm's Alex Katouzian to Lead Client Computing and Physical AI Group

key_facts.fact: Intel appointed Alex Katouzian as executive vice president and general manager of Client Computing & Physical AI, a new group combining its core PC business with robotics, autonomous machines, and edge AI.

Katouzian spent more than 20 years at Qualcomm, most recently as EVP and group general manager of mobile, compute, and extended reality (XR), and is the second senior Qualcomm hire by Intel after GPU architect Eric Demers.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Katouzian will help 'reimagine client computing beyond the traditional PC and align this future with the next wave of growth in physical AI.'

Intel also confirmed Pushkar Ranade as permanent CTO, transitioning from interim role; he will continue as chief of staff to CEO Lip-Bu Tan and lead quantum, neuromorphic, photonics, and novel materials work.

stories.headline: Lattice Semiconductor to Acquire AMI for $1.65B, Targeting $1B+ Annual Revenue by Q4 2026

key_facts.fact: Lattice Semiconductor will acquire AMI, the leader in platform firmware and infrastructure manageability for cloud and AI, for $1.65 billion ($1B cash and ~$650M in stock).
AMI is expected to generate over $200 million in revenue in 2026 and the deal supports Lattice's trajectory toward $1 billion+ annual revenue run rate by Q4 2026.
Lattice reported Q1 2026 revenue of $170.9 million, up 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.41 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 39.6%.
The combination creates what Lattice calls the industry's most complete secure management and control platform, addressing datacenter modularity, complexity, uptime, and deployment challenges.

AMI is majority owned by THL Partners and the deal is expected to close in Q3 2026, with Lattice planning to fund the cash portion via balance sheet cash and new senior secured credit facilities totaling up to $1.15B.

stories.headline: Nscale to Invest €695M in Portugal, Deploy 66K+ Nvidia Rubin GPUs for Microsoft Starting Late 2027

key_facts.fact: Nscale will deploy 66,000+ Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs at the SINES Data Campus in Portugal for Microsoft customers, starting in late 2027.
The agreement includes €230 million in shared infrastructure and €465 million in a second 200MW building at the SINES Data Campus, totaling €695 million.
This builds on an initial deployment of 12,600+ Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs at the first building of the SINES Data Campus for Microsoft.
Start Campus is fully permitted for 1.2GW of capacity, positioning Portugal as a strategic gateway for Europe's AI economy.
Nscale's deployment is described as one of the largest Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 GPU installations in the EU, supplementing existing Nscale deployments for Microsoft in Norway, the UK, and the US.

stories.headline: Kuo: OpenAI Fast-Tracking AI Agent Phone With Custom MediaTek Chip, Mass Production H1 2027

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports OpenAI is fast-tracking its first AI agent phone, with mass production targeted as early as H1 2027, accelerated from prior 2028 timeline
MediaTek is currently the leading candidate as sole processor supplier, with a customized Dimensity 9600 chip built on TSMC's N2P (2nm) process node in H2 2026
The device features a dual NPU architecture for layered AI computing, LPDDR6 RAM, and UFS 5.0 storage to handle continuous on-device AI workloads
The phone is designed around AI agents rather than apps — users express intent and agents handle tasks directly, replacing the traditional app-based interaction model
Potential drivers include supporting OpenAI's year-end IPO narrative and intensifying competition in AI agent phones; shipments could reach 30 million units across 2027-2028

stories.headline: Palantir Reports 85% Revenue Growth to $1.63B in Q1, Raises FY26 Guidance to 71% Growth

key_facts.fact: Palantir reported Q1 revenue of $1.63 billion, up 85% YoY (its fastest growth since going public in 2020), beating estimates of $1.54 billion
US commercial revenue surged 133% YoY to $595 million; US government revenue grew 84% YoY to $687 million
Palantir raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $7.65-$7.66 billion (71% YoY growth), up from prior guidance of $7.18-$7.20 billion, above $7.27B consensus
CEO Alex Karp said Palantir's Rule of 40 score reached 145%, and predicts the US business will double again in 2027
Adjusted EPS was $0.33 vs $0.28 expected; GAAP net income quadrupled YoY to $870.5 million (53% margin)
Palantir closed 206 deals worth over $1 million, 47 deals exceeding $10 million, with total contract value of $2.41 billion (up 61% YoY)

stories.headline: Panthalassa Raises $140M Led by Peter Thiel to Power Floating Data Centers With Ocean Waves

key_facts.fact: Panthalassa raised $140M led by Peter Thiel at a $1B valuation to develop floating data centers powered by ocean wave energy
The company aims to harness untapped ocean energy resources thousands of miles from human settlements to power AI infrastructure
VSC Ventures also participated in the round; the company was described as one of their 'coolest investments'

stories.headline: Panthalassa Raises $140M Led by Peter Thiel for Ocean Wave-Powered AI Inference at Sea

key_facts.fact: Panthalassa raised $140 million in Series B financing led by Peter Thiel, valuing the company at nearly $1 billion, to build autonomous floating platforms that generate electricity from ocean waves for AI inference.

Other investors include John Doerr, Marc Benioff's TIME Ventures, Max Levchin's SciFi Ventures, Hanwha Group, Super Micro Computer, Dylan Field, and returning backers Founders Fund and Lowercarbon Capital.

The nodes are autonomous floating steel structures that generate electricity from waves, use it on-board to power AI inference chips, and send results to land via satellite, with free ocean cooling eliminating traditional data center cooling challenges.

The funding will complete a pilot manufacturing facility near Portland, Oregon, and accelerate deployment of Ocean-3 series nodes in the northern Pacific Ocean in 2026, with commercial deployments targeted for 2027.
Lowercarbon Capital claims the system could generate power at roughly two cents per kilowatt-hour.

stories.headline: SAP Acquires Prior Labs With €1B Commitment to Build Europe's Leading Frontier AI Lab for Tabular Data

key_facts.fact: SAP entered a definitive agreement to acquire Prior Labs, committing to invest more than €1 billion over four years to scale it into a globally leading frontier AI lab for structured business data
Prior Labs built TabPFN, a tabular foundation model with over 3 million downloads, purpose-built for structured data predictions where LLMs struggle
SAP also announced the acquisition of Dremio, a data lakehouse platform with $300M+ in prior funding, to enhance its Business Data Cloud offering
Prior Labs will continue operating independently, retaining its Freiburg, Berlin, and New York locations, and maintaining its open-source strategy
Prior Labs' cofounders Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir work with leading scientists including Yann LeCun

stories.headline: Sierra Raises $950M Series E at $15.8B Valuation, Serves 40% of Fortune 50 With AI Agents

key_facts.fact: Sierra raised $950 million in a Series E led by Tiger Global and GV (Google Ventures), at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation, up from $10 billion in 2025
Sierra now serves over 40% of the Fortune 50 and surpassed $150 million in annual recurring revenue in just eight quarters
CEO Bret Taylor estimates $400 billion is spent annually on customer service, with most of that shifting to AI agents
Sierra uses a 'constellation of models' from OpenAI and Anthropic alongside its own fine-tuned proprietary layers
Customers include Prudential, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Rocket Mortgage, and one in three of the world's largest banks
Sierra launched Ghostwriter in April, an 'agent as a service' tool that autonomously creates and deploys specialized agents from natural language descriptions

stories.headline: Trump Admin Considers EO to Vet AI Models Before Release, Reversing Hands-Off Stance

key_facts.fact: The White House is discussing an executive order to create a working group of tech executives and government officials to examine potential review procedures for new AI models before public release
Senior administration officials briefed executives from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI on some of the plans in meetings last week
The immediate catalyst was Anthropic's Mythos model, whose cybersecurity vulnerability-finding capabilities prompted national security concerns
The shift follows David Sacks' departure as White House AI czar in March; Susie Wiles and Scott Bessent have taken over AI policy
Critics say this amounts to a de facto licensing regime; ITIF president Daniel Castro called it a 'full embrace of the precautionary principle'

stories.headline: US Confirms 25% Tariff on EU Cars, Breaking Trade Deal; EU Finance Ministers Warn of Retaliation

key_facts.fact: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told EU and German trade officials the US will move forward with raising EU car tariffs to 25% from the agreed 15%
Trump announced the tariff hike on Friday May 1, claiming the EU had not complied with their trade deal reached in August 2025 at Turnberry
European Commission rejected Trump's claim of non-compliance, arguing the EU is still going through its legislative process to ratify the deal
EU finance ministers said all retaliatory options are on the table; German Vice-Chancellor Lars Klingbeil said 'we would be prepared if an escalation were to occur'
The tariff hike came amid US-EU tensions over the Iran war; the White House also announced plans to remove 5,000 US troops from Germany
Shares in Porsche, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen all fell 2-3% on Monday; the pan-European automobiles index dropped 2.3%

stories.headline: US Forces Open Hormuz Lane, Sink 6 Iranian Boats; UAE Hit by Missiles for First Time Since Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: US military fired on Iranian forces and sank six small boats targeting civilian ships as it moved to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Monday May 4
Two American-flagged merchant ships successfully transited the strait on Monday under a new US-led initiative
UAE air defenses engaged 15 missiles and 4 drones fired by Iran; a drone struck a Fujairah oil facility, wounding three Indian nationals
Adm. Brad Cooper said US forces opened a passage through the strait free of Iranian mines and defeated 'each and every' threat launched at civilian ships
Iran's foreign minister warned both the US and UAE 'should be wary of being dragged back into quagmire'; Iran called the incident a result of 'US military adventurism'
US and Gulf Arab nations are drafting a new UN Security Council resolution to condemn Iran for blocking the strait, co-drafted by US and Bahrain with Saudi, Qatar, UAE and Kuwait input
Iran's latest ceasefire proposal calls for US lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, withdrawing forces from the region, and ceasing all hostilities including Israel's operations in Lebanon
